pieces.file: Christopher Alexander — rich — a palace is not a tree.png
pieces.title: A palace is not a tree
pieces.caption: Three hubs and eighteen pages, drawn twice. On the left each page is filed under one parent. On the right every real tie between a page and a hub is kept, and the red pages belong to more than one. *What is real and what is a choice:* Eighteen of the hubs' 123 neighbours, ten of them picked from the 24 that touch more than one hub, so overlap is over-shown: about one page in five really overlaps. Which hub keeps a page on the left is the drawing's choice. Ties among the eighteen are left out. The title is the piece's claim; the page says cities are semi-lattices. *Leaking in:* The three hubs are the palace's biggest, not his neighbours: none of them links his page.

verdicts.file: Christopher Alexander — rich — a palace is not a tree.png
verdicts.why: Words only; the picture can stay. The caption's "every real tie is kept" is not so: only page-to-hub ties are drawn (the hub-to-hub link Spinoza Conatus → Kuramoto Coupling and all ties among the eighteen are left out; the in-image footer says it correctly). And the honesty line does not own the pick: the eighteen are ten of the 24 overlapping pages plus eight single-hub ones, chosen from 123 neighbours, so 56 percent of what is shown overlaps where 20 percent really does.
